//: The Bash split a permission's binding rests on, shared by every port: tstack fleet/src/ledger/permission.ts (simpleCommands, scriptsOf, whyNoAsks, runsOf), the hook hooks/tstack-hook.py (_rule_commands, scripts_of, why_no_asks, runs_of), and the fleet repo's packages/ledger/src/permission.ts and fleet-host's grant-writes.ts, which copy this file byte for byte and pin it by sha256. A case is a call; `$FIXTURE` stands for a folder that holds `fixtures` (a file's path in it, its folders made, to its text), and is put in every string before the case runs, a fixture's text too. `commands` is the split, `scripts` the script each simple command names (in order, repeats kept), `whyNoAsk` null when the call can be asked for or a substring of the refusal whyNoAsks gives for [call, ...more], and `runs` what runsOf gives for [call, ...more] (a script's file, and the .fleet/ws-pre-remove hook a `fleet ws DIR trash NAME` runs, by its sha256, or by 64 zeros, the absence entry, when the repo has no such file). A case with `appears` writes those fixtures after `runs` is checked: the port's check at the yes (tstack's whyRunsMoved, the hook's _moved_file, the host's grantOf) then gives a refusal that holds `appeared`, and the files go again. A case with `unreadable` has those fixtures made mode 000 for the case and given their mode back after (a port that runs as root, which reads them anyway, skips the case). A case with `since` is a hole of the design review closed by that patch (F3, F11), or a call round 6 holds to its rule (R6): a page ask holds a call only of the programs it knows, whose words name what runs. `$FLEET_CLI` stands for the plugin's own fleet CLI, fleet/bin/fleet of the checkout the port runs from (the fleet repo's ledger, which reads no file, any absolute path; its host, a file it writes), and `$FLEET_SHA` for that file's sha256. `isolate`, where a case has it, is the substring the fleet repo's ledger port gives in place of `whyNoAsk`: it runs in the cloud's isolate, where no file can be read, so it refuses any absolute `…/fleet`, and the hook and tstack's CLI, which read the disk, decide such a grant. A `//` on a case says why it stays as it is. Change every port and this file together.

cases.whyNoAsk: /locked/.fleet/ws-pre-remove cannot be read, so the card cannot bind the file trash runs

cases.name: a $ in single quotes is read as written
a $ in double quotes expands when it runs
cases.whyNoAsk: `$HOME` has a $

cases.name: a $ outside quotes expands, next to a single-quoted one
cases.whyNoAsk: `$HOME$PATH` has a $

cases.name: a single quote in double quotes quotes nothing, so its $ expands
cases.whyNoAsk: `'$HOME'` has a $

cases.name: git takes a refused long flag by a unique prefix: the pager of grep
cases.whyNoAsk: `git --open-files=./x` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: git takes a refused long flag by a unique prefix: the remote's pack program
cases.whyNoAsk: `git --upl=./x` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: git push takes --receive-pack by a prefix
cases.whyNoAsk: `git --rece=./x` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: git clone is no ask: its -u is --upload-pack, and a template's hooks run
cases.whyNoAsk: `git clone` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: git's -c after the subcommand is the subcommand's own
cases.//: git reads -c <name>=<value> as its own only before the subcommand: git grep -c counts, git switch -c makes a branch

cases.name: git's -c before the subcommand, past another global option, still sets config
cases.whyNoAsk: `git -c` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: a pnpm subcommand is the first word past its flags and their values
cases.//: pnpm --filter x test runs the test script of package x: x is the filter's value, not pnpm x

cases.name: pnpm exec past a filter is still pnpm exec
cases.whyNoAsk: `pnpm exec` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: a fleet refused word in a message is a word of the message
cases.//: fleet tell FLEET TEXT...: the text is told, not run

cases.name: jj config set writes what a later jj call runs
cases.whyNoAsk: `jj config` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: gh config set writes what a later gh call runs
cases.whyNoAsk: `gh config` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: npm config set writes what a later npm call runs
cases.whyNoAsk: `npm config` runs code the call does not name

cases.name: fleet preview with no subcommand names what is missing
cases.whyNoAsk: `fleet preview DIR` needs its subcommand, status or stop
